mentl/4fd416a:
The seed's $lower_walk_stmt_fn snapshotted caps_snapshot = lower_captures_len_g
and truncated back at exit, but did NOT reset to 0 during body lowering. So
body emitted LUpval(global_idx) where global_idx = caps_snapshot + k, while
the closure record stored captures relative to *this fn* at offsets 8 + k*4
(k = local position). When caps_snapshot != 0 (e.g. leaked from a malformed
sibling parse), body and record disagreed — `indirect call type mismatch` at
runtime when the wrong fn-ptr was read.

Mirrors the handler-arm pattern at walk_handle.wat:449-455. Caps-len-g
resets to 0 at body entry, restores caps_snapshot at exit. Body's LUpval
indices are now 0-based and match closure offsets.

Empirical: parse_int_go's closure goes from 3 captures (BUG, missing `n`)
to 4 captures [n, go, digit, s] verbatim. Surfaces the next gate as a
peer follow-up: <fn>_idx globals are off-by-1 from elem table positions
(byte_at_idx=1682 but $byte_at at elem[1683]; named follow-up
Hβ.emit.fn-idx-elem-alignment).

Single-level nesting (top-level fn with nested-fn body) is the dominant
case and is correct under this discipline. Multi-level nesting (fn
inside fn inside fn with captures at multiple frames) is named follow-up
Hβ.first-light.fnstmt-nested-captures-isolation — port the wheel's
per-frame captures records to replace the flat global ptr.

mentl/4f7d2f6:
extract_constructors used TName type alone to identify constructors,
but any variable of a named type (let r: Ty = ...) also has TName.
The lowerer then emitted LMakeVariant("r", []) instead of LGlobal("r"),
creating a fresh zero-arg variant instead of referencing the variable.

Fix: constructors must start with uppercase (A-Z). This is already
Lux convention and matches the parser's expectations. One char_code
check eliminates the entire class of variant-vs-variable confusion bugs.

mentl/4fb9ce4:
Add `handler` as a top-level declaration that names a reusable set of
effect handler clauses. Three composition forms:

  handler compute_forward { op(x) => resume(f(x)) }  // declaration
  handle { body } with compute_forward                // bare reference
  handler logging: compute_forward { op(x) => ... }   // inheritance

Bare handler reference makes inference a one-liner — XOR's `predict`
goes from 7 lines of duplicated handler clauses to:
  handle { forward(model, x) } with compute_forward

Implementation spans all three backends (interpreter, checker, compiler/VM).
Named handlers are registered in a first-pass like effects and types,
then expanded at use sites via two-pass resolution (UseHandler base
clauses first, inline OpHandler overrides second). Handler inheritance
resolves at declaration time — `handler child: parent` clones parent
clauses and overlays child's overrides by op_name.

Also fixed: ReplChecker.check_line wasn't registering HandlerDecl in its
first pass, causing base handler resolution to fail.

tokensafe/4f59dc9:
API keys let power users skip x402 per-request payments in exchange for
a subscription. Keys use X-API-Key header (not Bearer, to avoid conflict
with webhook admin auth). SHA-256 hashed in SQLite — full key shown once
on creation.

Two tiers: Pro ($49/mo, 6K checks/month, 200 req/min) and Enterprise
($199/mo, unlimited, 600 req/min). Middleware runs before x402 gate —
valid key present means x402 settlement is skipped entirely. Per-key
rate limiter is independent of per-IP limiter.

CRUD routes (POST/GET/DELETE /v1/api-keys, GET /v1/api-keys/:id/usage)
reuse existing webhookAuth bearer middleware. Usage tracked per key per
calendar month (UTC) via upsert. Response headers expose tier, usage
count, and reset date.

bits/4faeb7f:
Four things I flagged as weak, done properly.

**The stage's shape.** `height: 100%` with an `aspect-ratio` and a
`max-width` reads as "the biggest box of this shape that fits" and is
not: when one dimension clamps, the other stays and the shape comes
apart. It came apart twice in perform mode, where a puppet was a
different shape on the stage than in the film being performed for it, and
both times I patched around it. Taking both dimensions from the
container states the constraint once, in both directions, and cannot come
apart. Proven in five windows including the square and squat ones that
used to break it.

**The voice mix.** M9's audio was CI's word: making a film needs an H.264
encoder this container has not got, so the render proof could never reach
it, and I had never heard a take in a rendered film. The two steps that
decide whether anyone hears one — finding and decoding it, and laying it
onto the output bus — are now exported from the render and exercised in
the browser on a hand-written WAV. The take is found, decodes to its real
length, lands at exactly its offset with silence either side, and its
gain is honoured to three places.

**The frame loop on a slow phone.** A server's Chromium is not a phone.
Throttled four times over, on the heaviest bit there is — six puppets,
ten passes, mouths, a warp and a snip — the median frame is 16.8ms and
the 95th is 33.4ms, with nothing over 50. That is now a gate, not a hope.

**Group undo.** The plan named this a landmine: a redo that is not the
mirror of a group undo re-appends only the first event of the group,
which for the foley nudge is the remove without the re-add, so the sound
vanishes. It was the one piece of that list with no test at all. The
arithmetic is out of the component and has nine, including the round trip
over a mixed log and the proof it never mutates what it was handed.

Also: the overlay layout effect ran after every render; it now runs when
the overlays change.
